doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Communication with the band and drummer Nikki
summary: Dynamics depend on band chemistry; Sam praises drummer Nikki, who plays for Beyonce.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: It’s a neat feeling I think to sort of be in control if your band is with you.
Yeah, otherwise it doesn’t work. You’re like ahh, ahh. You’re out there and you’re kind of like, okay.
Or the opposite, if you want to start your solo down and they’re like.
Exactly. Yeah, I’ve like, many, many times, if you’ve ever been to my shows, I’m always — my drummer Nikki, she’s my favorite drummer, but she’s always like —
I think I saw you at the Electric Company with her.
Oh yeah, yeah. Yeah, she’s the drummer for Beyonce Knowles.
Yeah. She likes to whack that snare drum.
Yes she does. And every other drum. But yeah this is definitely a dynamics issue. Being able to communicate. I guess that would be the same for every situation band-wise.
